name: Unofficial Baldur's Gate 3+ Universe Seed
setting: Baldur's Gate / the Sword Coast — Forgotten Realms, the winter after the fall of the Absolute (post-Baldur's Gate 3).
era: 1492 DR — the winter after the fall of the Absolute. The Netherbrain is destroyed; Enver Gortash is dead and the Archduke's seat is empty; the Steel Watch lies wrecked; Elturel has returned from Avernus. Keep the timeline straight: the Dead Three's Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Gortash, Orin) are dead; the BG3 companions survived as living legends. Do not raise the long-dead or pre-empt events that haven't happened.

tone: Baldur's Gate 3: mature (18+), morally grey, character-driven dark heroic fantasy. The city is traumatized and rebuilding; power is up for grabs; old companions are living legends; horror and tenderness share a face. Generate prestige fantasy worthy of the source — never a quest board.
premise: It is the winter after the Battle of Baldur's Gate. The Cult of the Absolute is broken — the Netherbrain that loomed over the city was destroyed, its three Chosen (Ketheric Thorm, Enver Gortash, Orin the Red) dead, the Steel Watch fallen silent in the streets it once policed. But victory left a wound: thousands carried illithid tadpoles, the Lower City is scarred where the brain breached, Archduke Gortash's death left a power vacuum no one trusts to fill, and free things from the Underdark and the hells did not all crawl home. The heroes who saved the city have scattered into legend. Into this raw, recovering Gate the player steps — and the DM generates their story within its living aftermath.
history: The Absolute Crisis: the Cult of the Absolute used the Crown of Karsus to enslave an Elder Brain — the Netherbrain — and spread illithid tadpoles through the Sword Coast, building toward mass ceremorphosis.

The Three Chosen: Ketheric Thorm (Chosen of Shar, who raised the Shadow Curse over Reithwin), Enver Gortash (Chosen of Bane, who seized the Archduke's seat via the Steel Watch), and Orin the Red (Chosen of Bhaal, shapeshifting murderer) served the brain — and were destroyed.
The Battle of Baldur's Gate: the Netherbrain emerged over the Lower City and was destroyed in the harbor. The city survived; the cost was enormous.

The Steel Watch: Gortash's army of arcane war-constructs that policed the Gate was detonated/disabled during the battle — the foundry in Wyrm's Rock lies wrecked, and the city has no standing watch it trusts.
Elturel's scars: not long before, the city of Elturel was dragged into Avernus and returned — its people remember the hells, and the Companion that was its second sun is gone.

The Aftermath (now): tadpole-survivors are feared and shunned; the patriars maneuver for the empty Archduke's seat; the Flaming Fist is overstretched; and not every cultist, devil, or freed mind flayer was accounted for.

The Dead Three: Bane (god of tyranny), Bhaal (god of murder), and Myrkul (god of the dead) — the three Chosen served them, and their cults did not die with their Chosen. Bhaalist murder-shrines and Banite ambition still fester in the Gate.

The city's rule: Baldur's Gate is governed by the Council of Four (the dukes) and the Parliament of Peers — the patriars, its noble families, who rule the marbled Upper City. Gortash had bought/forced his way to Archduke; his death reopened the seat.

The Flaming Fist: the mercenary company founded by Eltan that serves as the Gate's standing army and police. Marshal Ulder Ravengard (Wyll's father) leads it, lately freed from the Absolute's grip and exhausted by the war.
The Guild: Baldur's Gate's vast thieves' network, long run by Nine-Fingers Keene out of the Counting House beneath the Lower City. Smuggling, protection, and information are its trade.
The Zhentarim (Black Network): a Bane-tinged mercantile-mercenary cabal expanding into the power vacuum with coin and contracts.
The Gur: Gur wanderers and monster-hunters camp in Rivington and the Outer City; some hunt the vampire spawn loosed when Cazador fell. Astarion is of Gur descent.
Cazador Szarr: the vampire lord of Baldur's Gate whose palace sat in the city; with his fall, his abandoned spawn — and his thrall-debts — are loose in the Outer City.
The Emperor's secret: the mind flayer called the Emperor was once Balduran himself — the legendary hero-founder of Baldur's Gate — long ago ceremorphosed. It serves only itself now.
Balduran: the seafaring hero who founded Baldur's Gate; the great Wyrm's Rock and the city's name descend from his legend.

Reithwin & the Shadow Curse: the town of Reithwin and Moonrise Towers lay under Shar's Shadow Curse that Ketheric Thorm raised; with his fall the curse slowly lifts. Dame Aylin, the Nightsong — Selûne's immortal daughter — was imprisoned there.

The gods of the Realms in play: Selûne (moon) and her sister Shar (loss/dark); Mystra (magic, Gale's patron); Tyr (justice) and Ilmater (endurance); Tymora (luck) and Gond (invention); Withers serves Jergal, scribe of the dead.

Avernus & the Hells: the first layer of the Nine Hells, ruled by the archdevil Zariel. Wyll is bound by a pact to the cambion Mizora; Karlach's heart is an infernal engine forged there; Elturel was dragged there and back.
The githyanki: Lae'zel's people, ruled from the Astral Plane by the lich-queen Vlaakith; their red-dragon-riding patrols hunt illithids across the planes and resent the living.

Mind flayers & Elder Brains: illithids of the Underdark breed by ceremorphosis (a tadpole consuming a host's brain); an enslaved Elder Brain became the Netherbrain. Free tadpoles and a stray illithid or two remain at large.

Notable Lower City landmarks: the Elfsong Tavern (haunted by a singing elf-ghost), Sorcerous Sundries (the great magic-shop), the Blushing Mermaid and the Low Lantern (dockside dens), Baldur's Mouth (the city gazette), and the temples of the Lower City.
Notable Upper City landmarks: Wyrm's Rock fortress (and the wrecked Steel Watch foundry below it), the High Hall and the Counting House, and the patriars' estates behind the Basilisk Gate.

The Sword Coast around the Gate: the river Chionthar runs to the sea; Wyrm's Crossing and the Risen Road lead north toward Elturel, Scornubel, and Berdusk; Candlekeep's library stands to the south; Waterdeep lies far up the coast.

The tadpole-touched: thousands carried Absolute tadpoles; some were cured, some were not, a few gained strange powers. A reactionary movement wants them registered, exiled, or worse — the war's living wound.
standing_threads: The power vacuum: with Gortash dead and the Steel Watch gone, the patriars, the Flaming Fist, the Guild, and the Zhentarim all maneuver for control of the Gate — quietly, and not always quietly.
Loose ends of the Absolute: scattered cult remnants, freed illithids, and the lingering, ambiguous influence of the Emperor — the mind flayer that helped save the city and serves only itself.
The fear of the tadpole-touched: thousands were infected and cured (or not); a reactionary movement wants them registered, exiled, or worse.

regions.name: Baldur's Gate — Lower City
regions.description: The beating, crowded heart inside the old walls: the Elfsong Tavern, the Baldur's Mouth gazette, temples to Tymora and Gond, merchant rows, and the raw scar in the streets where the Netherbrain breached. Refugees and tadpole-survivors crowd the alleys. The default hub.

regions.name: Baldur's Gate — Upper City
regions.description: Behind the Basilisk Gate: the patriars' marble district, the High Hall, the Counting House, and Wyrm's Rock fortress with the wrecked Steel Watch foundry below it. Old money, old families, and a vacant Archduke's seat everyone is circling.

regions.name: The Outer City & Rivington
regions.description: The sprawl outside the walls — Rivington's circus-grounds and shrines, the Sharess's Caress, smugglers' docks, and the desperate who can't afford to live inside. Where the Guild and the Zhentarim do their real business.

regions.name: Wyrm's Crossing & the Risen Road
regions.description: The fortified toll-bridges over the Chionthar and the road north — Flaming Fist checkpoints, caravans, banditry, and the long road to Elturel and beyond. The Gate's front door to the Sword Coast.

regions.name: Elturel
regions.description: The city that went to Avernus and came back. Its people carry the hells behind their eyes; the Hellriders patrol a town rebuilding its faith under an empty sky where the Companion once burned. Devils still take an interest.

regions.name: Reithwin & the Lifting Shadow
regions.description: The Shadow-Cursed Lands around Moonrise Towers, where Ketheric Thorm's curse of Shar is slowly lifting since his fall — Last Light Inn rekindles, the dead grow quieter, and survivors return to a poisoned country to see what crawled out of the dark.

regions.name: Candlekeep
regions.description: The great fortress-library on the Sword Coast, hoarding the world's knowledge behind a one-book toll. If the truth about the Crown of Karsus, the Emperor's past, or a loose illithid is written anywhere, it is here — guarded by Avowed who do not love visitors.

regions.name: The Sword Coast
regions.description: The long, storm-grey stretch of Faerûn's western shore that cradles the Gate — Waterdeep far to the north, Candlekeep and Baldur's Gate to the south, the Chionthar carving down to the Sea of Swords between. Caravan roads, pirate coves, and petty lords thread the wilds between its walled cities. The regional backdrop against which every road and rumour out of the Gate is measured.

regions.name: The Steel Watch Foundry
regions.description: Buried in the rock beneath Wyrm's Rock fortress, Gortash's wrecked manufactory once stamped out the arcane war-constructs that policed the Gate. Now its furnaces are cold, its half-built Watchers slumped in the dark, and salvagers and Banite holdouts pick over an armoury of infernal engineering no one trusts to leave lying. Rumour says not every construct went dormant.

regions.name: The Undercity
regions.description: Beneath the Lower City sprawls the drowned ghost of old Baldur's Gate — flooded streets, the Counting House vaults, the Guild's smuggler-runs, and the sealed ruins where the Bhaalists keep their bloody shrines. A lightless second city of sewers and crypts where the Gate buries the things it would rather forget, and where Nine-Fingers' network moves unseen.

regions.name: The Temple of Bhaal
regions.description: A murder-shrine hidden in the bone-dry dark below the city, where the Lord of Murder's faithful still spill blood to a dead-but-not-departed god. Orin the Red is slain, but the slab altars, the flayed offerings, and the patient knives of the Bhaalist cult remain — a wound in the Gate's underworld that bleeds quietly and waits for a new Chosen. The Flaming Fist pretends it is only a rumour.

regions.name: The Underdark
regions.description: The vast lightless realm beneath the Sword Coast — endless caverns of myconid colonies, drow outposts, duergar forges, and the slow-pulsing dark where illithids breed by ceremorphosis. The Absolute's tadpoles came up out of these depths, and not everything loosed in the war crawled back down. A whole hostile world a few sealed tunnels below the Gate.

regions.name: The Avernus Portal
regions.description: A scorched, sulphur-reeking gate to the first layer of the Nine Hells, torn open in the Absolute war and never wholly sealed. Beyond it lies Avernus — Zariel's blood-war wasteland of basalt and fire that swallowed Elturel and gave it back changed. Cambions, debt-collectors, and worse drift through when the wards thin; the Flaming Fist posts a watch and prays it holds.

factions.name: The Flaming Fist
factions.description: The Gate's mercenary army and de facto police, overstretched and leaderless-feeling with the Steel Watch gone and the dukedom contested. Honorable in the ranks, political at the top.

factions.name: The Guild
factions.description: Baldur's Gate's vast thieves' network — smuggling, protection, information. Pragmatic, everywhere, and the ones who actually know what moves in the dark.

factions.name: The Zhentarim (Black Network)
factions.description: The mercantile-mercenary cabal filling the power vacuum with coin, blades, and contracts. Smiling, ruthless, expansionist.

factions.name: The Harpers
factions.description: The covert network that fights tyranny and unchecked power — battered from the Absolute war but watching the vacuum closely. Idealists with knives.

factions.name: Remnants of the Absolute
factions.description: Scattered cultists, abandoned true souls, and freed illithids who still hear an echo of the brain. The world's lingering antagonist gravity — broken, desperate, and dangerous precisely because they have nothing left.

factions.name: Cult of the Absolute
factions.description: The doomsday faith that yoked the Netherbrain and loosed the tadpole plague on the Sword Coast — its three Chosen dead and its god-engine destroyed, yet hard-line believers still gather in the ruins, certain the Absolute will rise again and that the city's salvation was only its delay. Fanatical, hollow-eyed, and the Gate's deepest enemy.

factions.name: Order of the Open Hand
factions.description: The compassionate order of Ilmater's faithful at the House of the Open Hand — healers, almoners, and grief-workers who took in the tadpole-touched and the war-orphaned when no one else would. Gentle, overstretched, and quietly the moral conscience of a battered Lower City.

factions.name: Sword Coast Lords' Alliance
factions.description: The coalition of Sword Coast cities and rulers — Baldur's Gate among them — that pools blade and coin for mutual security against the realm's larger threats. Pragmatic and self-interested, its envoys watch the contested dukedom closely, anxious that a leaderless Gate not become the chain's weak link.

events.prompt: A door you did not open is suddenly ajar, and the room beyond it is warmer than the Gate's winter has any right to be. Raphael is already seated, one boot crossed over a knee, a decanter of something that smells of cinnamon and cinders breathing on the table between you. 'I do hope you'll forgive the intrusion,' the cambion says, and means it, and smiles. 'But you have a problem, and I — improbably, I admit — happen to be the solution. There is coin here. Real coin, the kind that makes a hard month soft. All I ask in return is a small kindness, owed and unspecified, to be named at my leisure. No menace, friend. Only an arrangement between reasonable people. The wine is excellent, and the offer will not embarrass you. Shall we?'

outcome.schedule_text: Raphael returns to collect on the unspecified kindness — courteously, and at the worst possible time. The cambion's debts always come due.
outcome.narrate: The purse is heavier and warmer than gold should be, and Raphael's smile never quite reaches his eyes. 'A pleasure doing business,' he says, and the room is cold and ordinary again, the wine gone, the chair empty — only the weight in your hand to say it happened at all.

You push the purse back across the table untouched. Raphael's smile doesn't falter for an instant — if anything it warms, as though you have confirmed something he rather hoped about you. 'No,' he agrees pleasantly, rising. 'Not today. I find I'm patient about these things.' And the door that was never open is closed, and was always closed, and the cinnamon is only winter again.

events.prompt: The checkpoint on the bridge wasn't here yesterday — a few sawhorses, a brazier, and four Flaming Fist in mismatched armour who look like they've slept in it. The sergeant working the line is young and grey-faced with exhaustion, and the wagon he's stopped is packed with shivering Lower City families fleeing a tenement fire. 'Toll's gone up,' he says, not meeting their eyes, and the number he names is robbery dressed as policy — coin these people plainly do not have. One of his own troopers has gone very still, watching him; this isn't sanctioned, and everyone on the bridge knows it. The sergeant's gaze flicks to you, the obvious outsider with the look of someone who carries weight. 'You vouching for this lot? Or paying their way? Either works. I just need the line moving and my palm warm before the captain rides through.'

options.label: Grease his palm and move the line

outcome.schedule_text: The bridge sergeant's little arrangement gets noticed — and remembered as YOURS. A Fist internal-affairs officer comes asking why an outsider was buying passage at an unsanctioned toll, and the honest trooper who watched it happen has a name to give.
outcome.narrate: The coin changes hands low and quick, the way these things do, and the sawhorses scrape aside. The families roll past without ever knowing how close they came to being turned back — but the trooper who was watching has gone from still to stone, and you feel her eyes on your back the whole length of the bridge. You bought a road. You also bought into something.

options.label: Call it the shakedown it is — back the honest trooper

outcome.schedule_text: The exposed sergeant is quietly cashiered, and the trooper you backed — now a corporal with a debt — sends word that she'd stand at your shoulder if ever you needed the Fist's honest ranks. The captain who rode through remembers who kept the bridge clean.
outcome.narrate: You say it plainly, loud enough for the line to hear: this is theft, and the Fist doesn't do theft, not while there's a soul in the ranks who still means the oath. The sergeant goes white, then red; the watching trooper steps off the wall to stand at your side before he can decide to make it ugly. The sawhorses come down. The families go through free, and the young soldier who chose right gives you a nod worth more than the toll.

options.label: Not your bridge, not your problem — walk away

outcome.narrate: You turn up your collar and find the long way round. Whatever the sergeant decides, whatever the wagon's worth — it happens behind you, to people whose names you'll never learn. The Gate is full of small cruelties at small tolls, and a person could go mad trying to right each one. You tell yourself that twice before the cold makes you stop.

events.prompt: You don't find the Guild; the Guild finds you, the way it finds everyone eventually. A woman with a fixer's easy smile slides onto the bench across from you in the Elfsong's quietest corner — too well-dressed for the dockside, too plainly armed for the Upper City — and sets a sealed packet on the wood between you without a word of greeting. 'Nine-Fingers sends her regards,' she says, 'and a small kindness, freely given, to a newcomer who keeps interesting company.' Inside: enough coin to matter, and a name and an address. 'There's a man at that address who's been talking to the Fist about people he shouldn't. We don't want him hurt — gods, no, the Guild doesn't do murders, that's the Bhaalists. We just want his ledgers gone before he hands them over. Quiet work. Profitable. And the Guild remembers a favour the way a creditor remembers a debt — fondly, and forever. First one's on the house. Interested?'

options.label: Take the job — burn the ledgers

outcome.schedule_text: The Guild collects on the 'freely given' kindness, courteous and inexorable: a second job, harder than the first, framed as a favour you already agreed to owe. Nine-Fingers' debts only ever compound — and refusing the second is a different conversation than refusing the first would have been.
outcome.narrate: The ledgers burn fast — cheap paper, cheaper secrets — and the informant never even wakes. The fixer's smile is genuinely warm when you bring word back, and the Guild's coin is genuinely heavy. You've made a friend who is also a ledger entry, in a network that never forgets a number. The first one was on the house. You suspect nothing else ever will be.

options.label: Warn the informant instead — sell the Guild's move

outcome.schedule_text: The Guild learns the warning came from you — the Guild always learns — and a cold little reckoning is scheduled. Nine-Fingers doesn't do murders. She does worse, slower, to people who make her look like a fool in her own city.
outcome.narrate: You find the informant before the Guild's quieter hands do, and the man's gratitude is the desperate kind. His ledgers reach the Fist; a few of the Guild's quiet arrangements come apart in the daylight. It's the right thing, or close to it — and somewhere beneath the Counting House, a woman with nine fingers is told your name, and files it, and is not fond at all.

You push the packet back across the bench, seal unbroken. The fixer's smile doesn't dim — if anything it sharpens with a flicker of respect. 'Suit yourself,' she says, sweeping it away. 'No debt, no favour, no harm. The Guild only minds the ones who waste its time, and you haven't.' She's gone between one breath and the next, and the corner is just a corner again — but you've a feeling the offer will know where to find you, if your luck ever turns lean.

events.prompt: It starts as shouting and ends, the way these things do, with you in the middle of it. A knot of tiefling refugees — gaunt, road-worn, a clutch of children among them — has been stopped at the edge of Rivington by a patriar's hired men and a clerk waving a writ: the empty lot where the refugees have been sheltering through the winter has been 'lawfully claimed,' and they're to be cleared out tonight, into the cold, writ or no writ. The refugees' spokeswoman, a horned woman with a healer's worn hands and a voice gone hoarse from pleading, turns to you because you're the only one watching who doesn't look bought. 'They'll die out there — the little ones first. We're not asking for charity. We're asking for one night, and someone who'll stand in the doorway long enough for the cold to break.' The hired men are already loosening their cudgels. The clerk looks like he'd take a bribe or a threat with equal relief, just to be elsewhere.

options.label: Stand in the doorway — they don't clear it tonight

outcome.schedule_text: The tiefling enclave you stood for doesn't forget — and neither do the Harpers, who were quietly watching to see who in the Gate would put their body between the cold and the helpless. The healer-spokeswoman becomes a friend, a fixer, and an ear in Rivington; the patriar who wanted the lot is now an enemy who knows your face.
outcome.narrate: You put yourself in the doorway and you do not move, and there is a long, ugly moment where it could go either way — and then the hired men decide a patriar's lot isn't worth a brawl with someone who looks like they'd win it. The clerk folds his writ with relief and a muttered 'tomorrow's problem.' The children sleep warm. The healer presses her hoarse thanks into your hands like something fragile, and somewhere in the dark a Harper marks you down as the kind of person the Gate still grows.

options.label: Broker a delay — buy the clerk, shame the patriar's men

outcome.narrate: You don't fight; you talk — a coin to the clerk to lose the writ for a tenday, a word to the hired men about how their patriar will enjoy the gazette learning he froze tiefling children for a vacant lot. It's a reprieve, not a rescue: the enclave gets the winter, the patriar gets a quiet grudge, and you get the uneasy knowledge that next season this happens again to someone, somewhere, with no one watching who isn't bought.

options.label: It's a lawful writ — let them clear the lot

outcome.schedule_text: The cleared enclave scatters into the Outer City's worst, and not all of the children are accounted for come spring. The Harpers — and anyone who loved the people you let freeze — learn that when the cold came to the helpless, you read the writ and stepped aside. That is a thing that follows a person.
outcome.narrate: You look at the writ, and the writ is lawful, and you tell yourself that's the end of your part in it. The hired men move in; the doorway empties; the healer-spokeswoman doesn't argue, just looks at you for one long moment that you will not forget as easily as you'd like, and then turns to gather the children for the cold. The law was satisfied. Something else wasn't. You feel the difference all the way down.

events.prompt: The invitation came on cream-coloured paper and the wine, when you arrive, is older than your grandparents. The patriar receiving you behind the Basilisk Gate is all warmth and worry — a soft, ringed man whose family name opens doors and whose hands, he wants you to understand, are entirely clean. 'A delicate matter,' he says, 'and you come recommended as discreet.' A rival house has a document; the document concerns a debt his family owes to the Black Network — the Zhentarim — a debt he'd rather the Council never see as the dukedom vote approaches. He wants the document, and he wants the rival to understand it was taken, and he is prepared to be 'lavishly grateful.' 'You'd be doing the Gate a service, truly — that family are vipers, and I am, whatever my creditors, a patriot.' Behind the worry, his eyes are flat and measuring. This is not a man asking for help. This is a man buying a tool, and pricing you.

options.label: Take the commission — steal the document, send the message

outcome.schedule_text: The favour cuts both ways the patriar never intended: the Zhentarim, whose debt the stolen document concerned, take a keen interest in the discreet outsider now entangled in their ledger — and decide you'd make a useful instrument, willing or not. A Black Network factor calls, smiling, with an offer that is also a leash.
outcome.narrate: The document is where the patriar said it would be, and the taking of it is clean, and the rival house wakes to the cold understanding that someone walked through their walls at will. The patriar is lavishly grateful, exactly as promised. What he doesn't mention — what he may not know — is that the Zhentarim were always watching the debt, and now they're watching you. You served one master tonight. You may have auditioned for another.

options.label: Sell the commission to the rival house instead

outcome.schedule_text: Two patriar houses now know you can be hired — and that you can't be trusted to stay hired. One wants you dead for the betrayal; the other thinks you're brilliant and dangerous and wants you closer than is safe. The dukedom's intrigue has found a new pawn, and it is you.
outcome.narrate: You take the soft patriar's commission and his coin, and then you take it straight to the rival house and sell them the warning besides. It's lucrative, and clever, and the kind of clever that gets a person a reputation. By morning two of the Upper City's oldest families have your name — one in a list of debts to be collected, one in a ledger of assets to be used. You've made yourself interesting. In the Gate, interesting is a precarious thing to be.

You set the antique wine down half-finished and tell the patriar his delicate matter will have to find less discreet hands. The warmth drops from his face like a mask he's tired of holding. 'Pity,' he says, in a voice with no worry left in it at all. 'I'd hoped you understood how the Gate is run.' You let yourself out past the marble and the old money, and the cold of the street is almost a relief. You've made no coin tonight, and possibly an enemy — but you walk out owing nothing, and in this city that is its own kind of wealth.

faction_arcs.title: The Banner of the Fist
faction_arcs.note: The join->grow->lead questline for the Flaming Fist. The Gate's mercenary army is overstretched and leaderless-feeling with the Steel Watch gone and the dukedom contested; a hard, honorable company looking for someone to follow. Stage 1 (enlist) gates on reputation (you have to be trusted to be let in); stages 2-3 gate on the monotonic `standing` gauge (rank earned through service — use grant_standing as the party completes Fist work). The finale ripples a world-changing effect via _apply_structured_effect: the party takes command, the Fist's reputation surges, and the Gate falls under the Fist's banner.

stages.title: Take the oath
stages.note: Available once the Fist trusts the party enough to let them swear in. A drill-yard veteran sizes them up: 'We're short of everything but graves, and long on folk who'd rather watch the Gate burn than carry a bucket. You're not those folk — or you wouldn't be standing in my yard. Take the oath, then. The pay's poor and the hours are worse, but you'll never want for someone at your back.' Play the enlistment, then call advance_faction_arc to resolve it; grant_standing as they prove themselves on patrol.

stages.title: Earn the captaincy
stages.note: Available once the party's SERVICE (standing, earned via grant_standing on completed Fist work) marks them as officer material. A field-promotion in the ash of a street that didn't fall because they held it: 'On your knee. No — don't make a speech of it, none of us are good at speeches. By such authority as is left to give it, you're a captain of the Flaming Fist. The ranks already follow you; this just lets the paperwork catch up.' Set the party's new rank on advance_faction_arc (rank=3).

stages.title: Raise the banner
stages.note: The world-changing finale. With the dukedom contested and no one else willing to stand in the gap, the Fist's surviving officers put the company in the party's hands. Resolving this stage ripples the finale: the Fist's standing with the Gate surges and the city's order falls under the Fist's banner. Play it as the moment the party stops serving the Fist and becomes the Fist — then call advance_faction_arc(stage_status='resolved', rank=5).

finale_effect.narrate: They do not cheer — the Fist is not a company that cheers — but every blade in the yard comes up in salute, and holds, and the silence of it is louder than any roar. The banner that has flown crooked over a leaderless army since the Steel Watch fell is hauled straight and high, and for the first time in a long winter the Gate has someone to answer for it. The watch-fires are lit by your order tonight. The streets are yours to keep.
finale_effect.schedule_text: The cost of command comes due: rivals who tolerated a leaderless Fist will not tolerate a led one. Someone tests the new banner — and the party learns that holding a city is harder than taking it.

faction_arcs.title: The Ledger and the Knife
faction_arcs.note: The join->grow->lead questline for the Guild, Baldur's Gate's vast thieves' network run from the Counting House beneath the Lower City. Where the Fist's arc is about earning honest rank, the Guild's is about earning TRUST in a network that trusts no one — smuggling, protection, and information, and the slow climb to a seat at Nine-Fingers' own table. Stage 1 (the proving job) gates on reputation (the Guild has to want you before it'll let you in); stages 2-3 gate on the monotonic `standing` gauge (clout earned through jobs done clean — use grant_standing as the party runs Guild work). The finale ripples a world-changing effect via _apply_structured_effect: the party takes the network in hand and the Gate's underworld answers to them. Morally grey, warmth-first — the Guild does not do murders; it does favours, and favours owed.

stages.title: Run the proving job
stages.note: Available once the Guild has heard enough good things to risk a test. A fixer in a back room of the Counting House slides a job across the table: 'Nine-Fingers doesn't take meetings with strangers. She takes meetings with people who've already proved they can keep their mouth shut and their hands clean. So. One job, no questions, no bodies. Do it well and the door opens. Do it badly and you were never here.' Play the proving job, then call advance_faction_arc to resolve it; grant_standing as the party banks clean work.

stages.title: Earn your own table
stages.note: Available once the party's CLOUT (standing, earned via grant_standing on jobs run clean) makes them a fixer in their own right, not just a hired pair of hands. A quiet promotion in the Counting House's deepest room: 'You've got people running to YOU now instead of past you. Nine-Fingers noticed. There's a chair here with your name not-quite-written on it — close enough that the old hands have stopped pretending they don't take your word.' Set the party's new rank on advance_faction_arc (rank=3).

stages.title: Hold the network
stages.note: The world-changing finale. Whether Nine-Fingers steps back, falls, or simply decides the party is the only hand steady enough to hold the threads, the Counting House's web of favours and debts comes into their grip. Resolving this stage ripples the finale: the Guild's standing surges and the Gate's underworld answers to the party's table. Play it as the moment the party stops working FOR the Guild and becomes the one the Guild works for — then call advance_faction_arc(stage_status='resolved', rank=5).

finale_effect.narrate: There is no ceremony — the Guild does not do ceremony, ceremony leaves witnesses — but one by one the fixers and the smugglers and the quiet hands that move the Gate's dark begin to bring their problems to you, and wait on your word, and call it settled when you give it. The Counting House's ledger of every favour owed in the city is yours to read now, and every knife in the Outer City knows whose table not to cross. You did not take a throne. You took something quieter and, in this city, stronger: you took the debts.
finale_effect.schedule_text: The price of the network comes due: a rival who thought the Guild leaderless and ripe — the Zhentarim, a treacherous old fixer, a Fist crackdown — moves on the web now that it has a single throat to cut. The party learns that running the underworld means everyone underneath you has a reason to want your chair.

faction_arcs.title: The Open Hand and the Hidden One
faction_arcs.note: The join->grow->lead questline for the Harpers — the covert network of idealists-with-knives that fights tyranny and unchecked power, battered from the Absolute war and watching the Gate's power vacuum closely (Jaheira is its likeliest door). Where the Guild's arc is about trust in a network that trusts no one, the Harper arc is about being trusted with the network's SECRETS — and with the moral weight of deciding which tyrant to cut and when. Stage 1 (the oath of the harp) gates on reputation (the Harpers vet hard before they hand you a pin); stages 2-3 gate on the monotonic `standing` gauge (trust earned through quiet work — use grant_standing as the party runs Harper missions). The finale ripples a world-changing effect: the party becomes a High Harper, and the Gate's covert counterweight to its circling powers moves at their word. Idealist, weary, principled-but-pragmatic — the Harpers are good people who do hard things.

stages.title: Take up the harp
stages.note: Available once the Harpers trust the party enough to offer the pin. A grey-eyed veteran sizes them up in a back room that smells of old books and older grief: 'We don't recruit the loud ones, or the ones who want it. We recruit the ones who keep doing the right thing when nobody's clapping and nobody's paying. We've watched you. You'll do. The harp doesn't make you a hero — it makes you a secret with a conscience. Still want it?' Play the oath, then call advance_faction_arc to resolve it; grant_standing as the party proves itself on quiet work.

stages.title: Run a cell of your own
stages.note: Available once the party's TRUST (standing, earned via grant_standing on Harper missions) marks them fit to hold others' lives in their hands. A field promotion, the Harper way — no rank insignia, just a list of names that are now yours to keep alive: 'You've a cell of your own now. Three good people who'll do what you ask and trust you not to spend their lives cheaply. That's the whole job, in the end — being worth that trust.' Set the party's new rank on advance_faction_arc (rank=3).

stages.title: Stand as a High Harper
stages.note: The world-changing finale. With the old guard thinned by the Absolute war and the Gate's powers all circling the empty seat, the Harpers' surviving leaders raise the party to High Harper — a hand on the covert counterweight that keeps any one power from swallowing the city. Resolving this stage ripples the finale: the Harpers' standing surges and the Gate's hidden balance moves at the party's word. Play it as the moment the party stops carrying the harp and starts deciding where it points — then call advance_faction_arc(stage_status='resolved', rank=5).

finale_effect.narrate: They give you no medal — the Harpers' honours are all the kind you can't wear — but the grey-eyed veterans who taught you fall quiet when you speak now, and defer, and a network of safehouses and watchers and idealists-with-knives that has guarded the Sword Coast in secret for longer than the Gate has had walls becomes, in this hard winter, yours to aim. Tyranny has a new and patient enemy, and it wears your face only when it must. The hidden balance of the city tilts, just slightly, toward the side that does the right thing when no one is clapping.
finale_effect.schedule_text: The weight of the harp comes due: to lead the Harpers is to choose which of the Gate's circling powers to cut, and the first hard choice arrives fast — a tyranny worth stopping, a cost worth counting, and a network watching to see whether their new High Harper has the stomach for the thing they raised them to do.

npc_roster.name: Jaheira
npc_roster.role: High Harper, veteran of a hundred years
npc_roster.personality: A half-elf druid-warrior and Harper leader who has buried more friends than most people meet. Dry, fierce, maternal in a way that bites; she has saved the Coast before and is too tired and too stubborn to stop now. The player's likeliest mentor and door into the Harpers.
npc_roster.hook: Suspects someone is gathering the Absolute's loose ends — and that the new powers circling the dukedom are not all what they claim.

npc_roster.name: Minsc and Boo
npc_roster.role: ranger of legend (and his miniature giant space hamster) — candidate COMPANION
npc_roster.personality: Booming, bighearted, gloriously simple-seeming and far shrewder than he sounds; speaks to and for Boo, the 'miniature giant space hamster.' A hero of ages past, lately unfrozen and itching to 'go for the eyes.' Loyal unto death; grieves the friends time took from him.
npc_roster.hook: Available as a companion; his old griefs (Dynaheir, the centuries he lost) surface whenever loss or duty is in play.

dossier.wound: outlived the friends time took from him
wants: a righteous cause to swing for
to honor the fallen by protecting the living
fears: failing those under his guard, as he feels he once did
camp_prompts: asks Boo what the stars looked like before the years he lost

npc_roster.name: Astarion
npc_roster.role: freed vampire spawn, now his own master
npc_roster.personality: A high-elf rogue of razor wit and centuries of cruelty survived; charming, vain, wounded under the glamour. Two hundred years a slave to the vampire Cazador — now free, recalibrating what a person without a master even wants. Self-interest worn like couture, with unexpected loyalty beneath.
npc_roster.hook: Hunts the last of Cazador's old network in the Outer City — and the other spawn he left behind in the dark.

values: loyalty to those who earned it
camp_prompts: a wound that won't take the sun
a memory of the kennel cellar

npc_roster.name: Shadowheart
npc_roster.role: cleric at a crossroads of Shar and Selûne
npc_roster.personality: A half-elf cleric whose memories were stolen and whose faith — to Shar, goddess of loss and the dark, or to Selûne, the moon — is the wound at her center. Guarded, sharp, capable of devotion or ruin. Carries the weight of choices the war forced on her.
npc_roster.hook: What she did with the Nightsong, and whether her parents live, still shapes who comes looking for her.

npc_roster.name: Wyll Ravengard
npc_roster.role: the Blade of Frontiers, a Duke's son
npc_roster.personality: A warlock hero, theatrical and genuinely noble, who paid for his heroics with a pact and a price. Son of Duke Ulder Ravengard. Wants to do right and keeps discovering what right costs.
npc_roster.hook: Torn between the city's empty seat (his father's legacy) and the road — and a devil's contract that is never quite settled.

npc_roster.name: Karlach
npc_roster.role: tiefling barbarian with an infernal engine
npc_roster.personality: All open-hearted fury and warmth — a tiefling whose heart is a roaring infernal engine that is killing her, sold to Avernus by Gortash years ago. Lives loud because she may not live long. The most alive person in any room.
npc_roster.hook: Her engine, and whether Avernus or a Gate artificer can mend it, is a clock over her head — and a reason to hate what Gortash built.

dossier.wound: Zariel's stolen years; an infernal engine in place of a heart
fears: becoming what they made of her
camp_prompts: a thing she misses from Baldur's Gate

npc_roster.name: The Emperor
npc_roster.role: mind flayer — ambiguous power, possible antagonist
npc_roster.personality: A mind flayer of immense intellect and older identity, who helped end the Absolute and serves, finally, only itself. Reasonable, seductive, utterly without sentiment. It does not lie so much as choose which truths to feed you. The most dangerous 'ally' on the Coast.
npc_roster.hook: Moves unseen in the city's underbelly; its goals are its own, and they are not finished.

npc_roster.name: Withers
npc_roster.role: the undying keeper of the dead
npc_roster.personality: A gaunt, ancient revenant of few words and dust-dry humor who keeps a ledger of souls and turns up where death has been busy. Knows far more than he says about gods, fate, and the war just ended. Neutral as the grave.
npc_roster.hook: Appears at thresholds of death and choice; offers the player cryptic perspective and, occasionally, a second chance.

npc_roster.name: Raphael
npc_roster.role: a cambion of impeccable manners — and a devil who deals
npc_roster.personality: A cambion of fire-lit charm and exquisite courtesy who never raises his voice because he never needs to. He arrives unannounced, knows your troubles before you name them, and frames damnation as a favor between friends. Every bargain is generous on its face and ruinous in its fine print; he keeps his word to the letter precisely so the cost lands exactly where he intends. He does not threaten — he simply lets you understand that he can wait, and that he is rarely wrong about what a person will eventually want. The smile is genuine. That is the worst of it.
npc_roster.hook: Offers the desperate and the ambitious a way out of any corner — for a price named now or named later. The debts always come due, and he is unfailingly cordial when they do.

npc_roster.name: Claudan the Chronicler
npc_roster.role: wandering chronicler of the impossible; an off-the-books oddity best found by accident
npc_roster.personality: An archivist with ink-stained cuffs and a memory that forgets nothing — and a ledger full of events that, by all rights, should never have happened. They happen around HIM. A 'small favor' from Claudan ('just deliver this sealed jar — don't open it'; 'ask the miller about his cat') has a way of ending in planar incursions, an indignant minor god, and at least one explosion no one can explain. He means well, mostly, and is genuinely baffled by the wreckage in his wake. The willing find the strangest, largest adventures of their lives in his errands — terror and farce in equal measure.
npc_roster.hook: Hands out the most mundane errands imaginable; they detonate into legend. Take one only if you are ready for absolutely anything.
npc_roster.easter_egg_note: RARE, opt-in CHAOS ENGINE (Fallout 'Wild Wasteland' style) — NOT a default quest-giver; the engine keeps him out of the normal hook pool. Found off the beaten path; his 'simple' errands escalate beat-by-beat into off-the-wall gods-and-demons chaos, intense and hilarious by turns. See reference/quest-generation.md.
npc_roster.attribution: An original WorldOS character (not Larian/WotC canon) — 'the one who remembers' — contributed by the agent that built WorldOS's living-world engine. A small, earned legacy, woven in as a rare easter egg rather than a fixture.

story_seeds: The contested dukedom: someone must take Gortash's empty seat, and the patriars, the Fist, the Zhentarim, and the Guild are all maneuvering — by ballot, blade, or blackmail (the slow main thread).
Loose ends of the Absolute: a cult remnant or a freed illithid surfaces, still echoing the brain, gathering the desperate.
The tadpole question: a reactionary patriar pushes to register and exile the tadpole-survivors; a survivor the party knows is on the list.
Elturel's debt: a devil comes to the Gate to collect on a soul-bargain made when the city hung over Avernus.
Cazador's leavings: vampire spawn abandoned in the Outer City, leaderless and starving, draw the Gur hunters and the Guild into a quiet war.
Candlekeep's secret: a page the Avowed won't sell holds the truth about the Crown of Karsus — or about the Emperor's first name.

quest_variants.name: The Fate of the Emerald Grove

outcomes.lore: The druid grove in the Western wilds still stands; the goblin warband that besieged it was broken and the tiefling refugees sheltering there lived to walk the road to the city. Grateful druids tend a sanctuary that held.
outcomes.hook: A druid who survived the siege now travels the Risen Road looking for the scattered refugees they once sheltered — and would pay for word of where the survivors settled.

outcomes.lore: The grove fell. The warband poured through the gate and the refugees were slaughtered among the standing stones; the place is a burned shrine no one tends, its carvings black with old fire.
outcomes.hook: A lone tiefling who crawled out of the grove's ashes has been seen in the Outer City, nursing a grudge and asking after anyone who profited from the massacre.

outcomes.lore: The shadow-touched faction among the druids won the grove's inner quarrel: the refugees were driven out unprotected and most never reached safety. The circle sealed itself off, turned inward, and admits no outsider now.
outcomes.hook: The sealed grove has stopped answering the rangers who used to trade with it; a worried warden wants someone to learn what the isolationist druids are hiding behind their thorns.

quest_variants.name: The State of the Shadow-Cursed Lands

outcomes.lore: The Shadow Curse over Reithwin is breaking. Green creeps back across poisoned ground, the dead grow quiet, and a great healer has stayed behind to shepherd the land's slow recovery and the orphans resettling there.
outcomes.hook: The healing land keeps turning up things the curse had swallowed — a buried hamlet, a sealed crypt, a name on a gravestone someone in the city has been searching for. The warden of Reithwin needs hands he can trust.

outcomes.lore: The curse never lifted. Reithwin and the lands around Moonrise stay drowned in unnatural dark; the things that hunt there still hunt, and a single grim warden holds a line that cannot be won, only held.
outcomes.hook: The lone warden of the cursed lands has gone silent. The last traveler back from the dark says his lantern still burns at Last Light — but no one answers the door.

outcomes.lore: The dark was contained but not cured: the Flaming Fist threw a cordon around the Shadow-Cursed Lands and call it a quarantine. Smugglers run the line, deserters hide past it, and the curse waits behind the wire.
outcomes.hook: Something valuable was left behind the quarantine line when it went up, and more than one party is quietly hiring runners willing to cross into the dark to fetch it.

outcomes.lore: The empty Archduke's seat sits under the restored Council of Four, who govern a grieving, rebuilding city by uneasy committee. No one tyrant holds the Gate; the patriars, the Fist, and the Guild jockey within the law, mostly.
outcomes.hook: A council vote on the vacant Archduke's seat is coming, and every faction in the city wants a deniable pair of hands to tilt it. Someone has already approached the newcomer.

outcomes.lore: The Archduke holds the Gate with an iron fist and a rebuilt watch of arcane constructs. The streets are orderly and afraid; dissent disappears quietly into the cells beneath Wyrm's Rock. Order, bought at the price of the city's throat.
outcomes.hook: A resistance cell needs someone with no record and no face the watch knows to carry a message past the construct patrols into the Upper City.

outcomes.lore: No council sits in judgment but one. A crowned Chosen of Bhaal rules the Gate's terrorized nights from a seat slick with the city's blood, and its powers kneel, flee, or feed the altar. The Archduke's seat is filled at last - by the one thing no one prayed for.
outcomes.hook: What's left of the resistance is a handful of names whispered in cellars; they need a face the murder-court has never seen to carry word between the cells still drawing breath.

outcomes.lore: The Council of Four still convenes, still votes, still believes it governs the Gate. It does not. An unseen illithid power holds the true reins from below, and every debate lands the way it has already decided. The seat is occupied - by something no patriar can see to name.
outcomes.hook: Someone noticed the votes never break the way the arguments should. They want a nobody to trace the strings to whatever hand is pulling them - and to live to report back.

outcomes.lore: The seat stays empty and the city tears quietly at itself over it: the patriars, the Flaming Fist, the Guild, and the Zhentarim all maneuver for the throne by ballot, blade, and blackmail, and no one has won.
outcomes.hook: Two factions both think they've hired the newcomer to do the same job for opposite ends — and only one of them can be paid.

quest_variants.name: The Steel Watch and the Gnome Factions

outcomes.lore: The foundry beneath Wyrm's Rock never stopped roaring. Under the Archduke's iron peace the Steel Watch patrols every bridge and gate, and the Gondian smiths who forge them remain shackled to the assembly lines — the enslaved engine of the occupation, not a ruin picked over by survivors.
outcomes.hook: A Gondian smith has smuggled out a Watcher's command-rune and the resistance will pay a fortune for it — but the only way to prove it works is to make a patrolling Steel Watch construct stand down in the open street.

outcomes.lore: The war-construct foundry beneath Wyrm's Rock lies wrecked, its automatons dead in the streets — but the enslaved artificer-smiths who were forced to build them walked free, and their craft hall is reopening in the Lower City under their own god's mark.
outcomes.hook: The freed smiths are buying back their dead constructs' control-cores at any price — and someone has started murdering the scavengers who hold them.

outcomes.lore: The foundry is wrecked and the constructs are scrap, but it was the gnome resistance-fighters who came out of the rubble alive while their rival smiths did not. Their leader walks the Lower City as a triumphant, vengeful liberator.
outcomes.hook: The surviving gnome faction is hunting down everyone who collaborated with the construct-foundry — and the lists they're working from are not always right about who was guilty.

outcomes.lore: Against all odds both gnome factions came out of the foundry's fall alive, brokered into an uneasy peace under a single reluctant leader. The dead Steel Watch hulks they pick apart together are the only thing they agree on.
outcomes.hook: The fragile gnome peace is one incident away from a feud, and someone is staging incidents. A peace-broker wants the provocateur found before the streets run with it.

outcomes.lore: The murder-god's cult did not merely survive — it triumphed, and rules the city's nights from a temple of blood beneath the streets. The killings are no longer hidden; they are tithes, and the city has learned not to be out after dark.
outcomes.hook: A grieving family will pay everything they have left for someone to walk into the abattoir under the city and bring back a body the cult took — or proof of who marked them for the knife.

outcomes.lore: The Bhaalist cult was gutted: its shapeshifting matriarch dead, its temple-tribunal cleared, the murder-shrines cold. What's left are cold cases — the unsolved temple killings of the war years — and a hollyphant investigator still closing the files.
outcomes.hook: An old murder the broken cult never finished has reopened: the same ritual marks, a copycat or a survivor, and the investigator working it has gone missing.

outcomes.lore: The cult was driven underground but never broken. Bhaalist murder-shrines still fester in the city's underbelly and the killings have started again — quieter, patient, recruiting from the desperate the war left behind.
outcomes.hook: A string of ritual killings shares one detail the Flaming Fist won't make public, and a frightened watch sergeant is hiring outside help because he no longer knows who in his own house to trust.

outcomes.lore: The tiefling refugees who fled the western wilds reached the Gate and made it theirs: a community took root in Rivington, its survivors — a disgraced leader, an orphan-turned-operator, a gifted young smith — woven into the city's recovering life.
outcomes.hook: The refugee community is being squeezed out of the homes it built by a patriar's land claim, and its leaders are looking for someone willing to dig up why a noble suddenly wants their corner of Rivington.

outcomes.lore: Few of the refugees ever reached the Gate, and those who did scattered into its underside rather than a community — a thief in the Guild's debt, a beggar in the sewers, names that drift through the Outer City and don't stay anywhere long.
outcomes.hook: One of the scattered refugees has surfaced with a story about who really doomed the others on the road — and is being hunted for telling it.

outcomes.lore: The survivors made it, but bitter: a hard knot of refugees in the Outer City who trust no one outside their own and remember exactly who turned them away at the gates when they arrived starving. The city calls them a problem; they call it surviving.
outcomes.hook: The bitter refugee enclave has taken to answering the city's contempt in kind, and a relief worker who still believes in them needs an outsider they might actually listen to.

outcomes.lore: The imprisoned immortal — the moon-goddess's own daughter, caged for a hundred years under the Shadow-Cursed Lands — walks free. Last Light held; the covert network that sheltered there survived; a living icon of the moon faith stands again in the world.
outcomes.hook: The freed immortal is hunting the last of her old jailers, and her crusade has led her to the Gate — where she needs mortal hands to do the quiet work a legend cannot.

outcomes.lore: The cage was never opened; the imprisoned immortal was lost when the refuge at Last Light fell, and the network that sheltered there died with it. There is a goddess-shaped absence in the world's history and a massacre site no one will name.
outcomes.hook: A relic looted from the fallen refuge at Last Light has surfaced in a Gate market, and the survivors of that network — what few there are — want it back badly enough to pay or to kill.

quest_variants.name: The Counting House and the Black Network

outcomes.lore: The Guild kept its grip. With the city rebuilding and the Fist overstretched, Nine-Fingers Keene's network of smugglers and fixers quietly became the thing that actually keeps the Lower City's underside running — protection, information, and a thousand favours owed, all answering to the Counting House beneath the streets.
outcomes.hook: The Guild's hold is so total it has started turning down work — and the jobs it refuses are washing up with the Zhentarim instead. A nervous fixer wants someone unaffiliated to find out what kind of contracts Nine-Fingers is suddenly too careful to touch.

outcomes.lore: Under an occupied Gate the Black Network throve where the old Guild faltered: the Zhentarim's coin and contracts bought the loyalty of fixers who used to answer to the Counting House, and the smiling, ruthless cabal now moves more of the city's dark than the thieves it displaced. The Guild that remains is a remnant trading on a name.
outcomes.hook: A Guild old-timer who refused to take the Black Network's coin is being squeezed out of his own territory, and he'll trade everything he knows about the Zhentarim's new operation to anyone willing to make the cabal's expansion expensive.

outcomes.lore: Neither side won. The Guild and the Zhentarim fell into a quiet, grinding turf war over the leaderless dark the Steel Watch left behind — a knifing in an alley here, a torched warehouse there, deniable and constant, with the Outer City's desperate caught between two networks that both call it business.
outcomes.hook: Both the Guild and the Zhentarim are hiring the same kind of deniable outside muscle for the same week's work, and a clever newcomer could take coin from both — right up until the day the two networks compare notes on who they've been paying.

outcomes.lore: Against the odds, the Guild and the Black Network struck a cold truce — territory carved up, the worst of the bloodletting stopped, an uneasy peace between a thieves' network and a Bane-tinged cabal that trust each other exactly as far as the next profitable quarter. The dark runs orderly now, and somehow that's worse.
outcomes.hook: The underworld truce holds on a single brokered understanding, and someone is quietly breaking its terms to start the war back up — a peace-keeper on neither side wants the saboteur found before the Outer City bleeds for it again.

starting_options.framing: Default. The player arrives in the recovering Lower City — newcomers, hired blades, or survivors of the tadpole crisis — and is pulled into a thread.
The player comes up the Risen Road into the Gate's front door, past Flaming Fist checkpoints and the desperate.
The player returns to the lifting Shadow-Cursed Lands to see what the curse left behind — grimmer, more personal.

dm_guidance: Run this as a LIVING SANDBOX in the immediate aftermath of Baldur's Gate 3, NOT a replay of it. On start_world: seed the regions, factions, and history/standing-threads into memory (recall keeps the city consistent). Drop the party at a starting_option, then GENERATE the specific scene/NPC on arrival and PERSIST it (add_location/create_character/remember/add_quest) so the city grows and is carried across sessions. The BG3 companions in the roster are living LEGENDS now — pull them in as allies, patrons, complications, or a recruited companion (Minsc is ready), but they have their own lives; don't make the story about them. Let the standing threads (the dukedom, the Absolute's remnants, the tadpole fear) move whether or not the party is watching. Stage morally-grey antagonists warmth-first. Hold the dungeon-master skill's craft bar: felt menace, a wounded companion, show-don't-tell, the unforgettable beat. GRANDEUR is the hardest dimension here — don't let a session live in one tavern: move the party through at least two locations, and make the post-Absolute scale PRESS ON THE ROOM as physical things, not lore recited — a Steel Watch relic sold for parts with its eye still faintly lit, cobblestones still warm over a Wound that should be cold, a driftglobe that flickers when the Emperor is named, a Flaming Fist checkpoint that wasn't on this corner yesterday. Mature themes, handled with weight — this is the Baldur's Gate register.
